newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says monthly steel output over 500,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Iran says monthly steel output over 500,000 tonnes.

text.p: Iran's monthly steel output has topped 500,000 tonnes, paving the way for the country to reach a targetted 6 million tonnes annual production, an Iranian minister said in remarks published on Monday.
Mines and Metals Minister Mohammad Hossein Mahlouji told the daily Iran that output reached 502,000 tonnes in the month to September 20, topping the half-million mark for the first time.
Mahlouji said the production, at two steel plants in Isfahan in central Iran and another in southwestern Ahvaz, showed annual capacity was now more than 6 million tonnes, the daily said.
Officials have said the target for steel production was 6 million tonnes in the Iranian year ending on March 20, 1997, up from about 4.3 million tonnes the previous year.
Iran has set a 240 billion rial ($137 million) budget to double annual iron ore output to 5 million tonnes at the Gol-e Gohar mine in southeastern Kerman province over 30 months.
Iran plans to raise annual steel output to 10 million tonnes by the end of its second five-year plan ending in March 2000. ($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state budget accounts)
